text:
Artturi Lehkonen has 15 goals in 21 games, among the top five scorers in the league, and Evan Rawal of the Denver Gazette noted he's now on Colorado's top line and its top penalty-kill unit. His agent, Rawal added, has to be smiling, and NHLRumors.com has asked whether he's pricing himself out of Colorado.

Enjoy it while it lasts, because the finishing won't. He's shooting 33%, against 14% last season, and has 15 goals on 8.8 expected. The Avalanche have also scored 9.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Some of this is real: his own chances, 1.34 expected goals per 60, are up from last season's 1.23, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 90th percentile for chances from the slot last season. He goes to the right places. They're just going in at a rate nobody sustains.

Colorado takes about 51% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, a bit below the team. Our talent range still projects about 36 goals, which would be a career year. The Stanley Cup winner from 2022 has earned the bigger role; the goal pace is the part to discount.
